chunks: And that which was narrated is: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the making up of the month of Ramadan, if he is unable to perform it in succession, he may break it up, and he said: 'He does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.'

His saying (peace be upon him): 'He does not make up the month of Ramadan during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah,' the meaning is if he is a pilgrim, because he is a traveler, and it is not permissible for the traveler to make up the month of Ramadan unless he stays or intends to stay in a town for ten days.

And that which indicates what we mentioned is what we previously presented regarding the permissibility of making up the month of Ramadan during Dhu al-Hijjah. As for that which indicates that it is not permissible to make up the month of Ramadan while traveling, it is what was narrated:

key_terms.عَشْرِ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up the missed days of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler make up the entire month of Ramadan during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that while missed Ramadan days may be made up non-consecutively, a traveler is prohibited from completing the entire makeup period during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. This restriction specifically applies because a traveler remains in a state of travel (safar) and cannot count days toward the makeup unless they intend to stay in one place for ten days, thereby transitioning to a resident status.
